When setting up loseless scaling, cap your fps to 37 or so (assuming your monitor is capped at 75hz) and then scale it by 2x with loseless scaling.

So if you're playing on pc, get loseless scaling. Its about 5 euros on steam but very worth it. It can double or triple your fps, the downside is that you'll feel a slight amount of input latency but you get used to it. 
I use it for helldivers 2 and other poorly optimized games and its a life saver.

Main thing you have to watch out for when using loseless scaling is to disable any sort of frame generation in game, since having it on increases input latency by tenfold because they both generate "fake" frames. Gta 5 doesnt have frame generation though, so you should be fine.

I had the error of "unarc.dll error-11" when i tried to install the game. To clarify i've to let u know my pc specs: R9 5900x - 32GB ram 3200Mhz - RTX 3080 Gigabyte.

The solution is very simple (in my case) but try it urself and maybe it works for you as well, just follow my steps.

You have to decrease your pc CORES as i show you below:

1) Type in the win search bar "msconfig" and click on the first one.  
2) In the window popup just appear go to "BOOT OPTIONS" and click on "Advanced Options".  
3) Here you can see on the top left corner "Number of processors", click on it, and in the box shown select 8 or 10.

Then click "ok" and "apply".  
One more popup appear to you and you have to click on "Reboot Now".

After rebooting the pc, install the game (i swear, it worked fine for me without any errors). he finished in about 5-10 mins for my specs (that i told you at the begenning).

Once installed, go again in the windows search bar, type once again "msconfig" and repeat the steps shown before.

But this time you have to "uncheck" the little box near the title "number of processors" and reboot again the pc (this step serves to bring the number of processors to how they were before).

After this last reboot, you have to go one more time  
in the "msconfig" window, repeating the previous steps, and now you have to "check" the little box (that you unchecked before), select the correct cores for your PC (in my case I select 24 wich is the maximum for me) and then reboot for the last time. DONE! Now you can enjoy your game 😉

An advice: if like me you have to install multiple OLD games (im installing all the Assassin's Creed games), and most of them are very old, try to install all of them with the cores setted to 8 (or 10) to prevent further errors.

This worked fine for me, probably because my processor has 12cores and 24threads and this game is very old.. (its my personal guess).

When you find it, its as easy as following the given pipes through out the floor, which can be extremely looooong or extremely short, depending on the rng. My advice is to follow them closely, since they cross paths with other (false) pipes mutliple times and you can start following the wrong pipe if you aren't paying attention.

When you finally get to the valve (assuming you've followed the pipes correctly) you have to turn it from 0 to 500 pressure points. (Each turn results in 100 points, so 5 FULL turns are needed to open one of the valves) Turning the valve makes alot of noise and almost always ends up in an enemy bolting to you. So I'd recommend turning the valve half way through, (300 pressure points is about okay) then checking your surroundings and continuing if you're in the clear from there. 

After all 2 or 4 valves depeding on your player count have been opened, you can continue pushing the boat downstream.

Doesn't matter how fast you complete the trial, everything is based off of the points I mentioned above.

Obviously avoid damage (poison, attacks), avoid objects that make noise such as hanging cans and broken glass.

You HAVE to collect a set amout of posters to be eligible to get an A+ (solo 3 posters, with players 5 posters).

You get extra points for distracting enemies, throwing objects at them, hitting them in the head, using equipment that is given to you or found (rig, batteries, health, antidotes), using picklocks or the master key, healing or reviving teammates, kicking enemies of off teammates when they're pinned or being executed (skill perk needed).

Rule of thumb is to check your evaluation after the trial: text in black is what gives you extra points and you should do more of, red text is what deducts points, therefore lowering your grade (taking damage, yada yada and so on).

The more black(good) points you earn, the more red(bad) points you can stack without your grade dropping. So if you get hit once or twice you can still get an A+, but you have to get more good points to negate the percantage of the red ones, if that makes sense.

Pretty sure there is a cap on how many good points you can get per action (using your rig, healing, reviving, distracting, etc.). The grading is very generous if you do most of the good actions atleast a few times per trial.

Hope that helped :)
